sentences.text:
on 9 August, 2024
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice C. V. Bhaskar Reddy
 Writ Petition No.20731 Of 2015
Order:

This Writ Petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, is filed by the petitioner seeking the following relief:
"....to issue a writ order or direction more particularly one in the nature of Mandamus declaring the proposed action of the respondents in attempting to create an access by formation of road to the 3rd respondent college through the land of the petitioner in Sy.No.156 and 157 of Kompally Village to reach Kotha gadi-Kompally main road without adhering to the due process of law under The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 is illegal arbitrary and violative of article 300A of the Constitution of India,
consequently direct the respondents to desist from any such activity without adhering to the due process of law..."
2. The petitioner claims to be the owner and possessor of land to an extent of Acs.10.27 guntas in Sy.Nos.156 and 157 situated at Kompally Village having purchased the same under 9 different registered sale deeds.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In proof of the same, the petitioner filed copies of pattedar passbooks, title deeds and pahanis of the year 2015.
Since the date of purchase, the petitioner is in actual possession and enjoyment of the subject land by raising guava plantation.

3. The grievance of the petitioner is that with an intention to provide road to respondent No.3-college, the respondents are forcibly dispossessing the petitioner from the subject land without following due procedure as enshrined in The Right to Fair Compensation and CVBR, J Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short, 'the Act').

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and CVBR, J Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In support of his contentions, the petitioner has filed some photographs showing levelling the land of the petitioner.

4. Respondent No.3 filed counter-affidavit stating that the photographs filed by the petitioner show that already there is an existing road and only for the purpose of clearing bushes to clean up the existing roads, respondent Nos.1 and 2 are taking steps but they are not interfering with the land of the petitioner and are not proceeding to form new road.

5. In view of the said submissions, this Court deems it appropriate to dispose of the writ petition directing the respondents to follow the due procedure as contemplated under the Act, if the land of the petitioner is required for formation of road or any other public purpose.
6. With the above direction, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
